records.text: Owens said Joint Task Force Six was a brand-new command created at the border around 1990 by President George H. W. Bush as part of the war on drugs.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was at the bottom of the military chain. He was just 20 years old, and he was put on what was actually a brand new command, the first ever Joint Task Force Six, and this new command was being created down at the border by President George H.W. Bush

verification.notes: Owens described JTF-6 as a brand-new command around 1990 and tied its creation to President Bush's border drug effort with Colin Powell's help. The cited JTF North command history confirms the origin and roles but dates the effective establishment order to November 13, 1989, so the legacy year is slightly inaccurate.

sources.title: CALL 10-52: Joint Task Force North History
sources.relevance: The reproduced JTF North command history dates the JTF-6 establishment order to November 13, 1989, ties it to President Bush war-on-drugs declaration, and identifies Colin Powell as issuing the order.

records.text: Harry Myers alleged that photographs in the Mexican-side tunnel house showed U.S. military and Border Patrol personnel posing with El Chapo and a tunnel architect
records.speaker: Harry Myers

appearances.snippet: where our Joint Task Commander, who was a high-ranking Border Patrol, was actually in the photos in that house posing with El Chapo and Felipe (architect; surname unverified), his architect, and there were other U.S. Marine officers and Mexican law enforcement officers and military that were in those photos, okay, end quote.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous tunnel reporting confirms the house, tunnel, JTF-6 detection team, and raid, but searches found no published photographs or official inventory matching the described images. Because the transcript is Owens reading Myers account, the speaker and conveyance were corrected and the image claim retained explicitly as his allegation.

conveyance.original_source: Harry Myers account read by Candace Owens

records.text: Harry Myers said a cartel member in Naco confirmed his identity by reciting personal details from his military clearance packet, which was supposed to be held by the Joint Task Force Six commander.
records.speaker: Harry Myers

appearances.snippet: In continuing the mission, me and one Border Patrol agent were sent to Naco, Arizona, where I was approached by a cartel member confirming my identification by rattling off my mother's name, address, my high school, my friends, everything listed in my clearance packet, which was supposed to be locked in custody, in the custody of the Joint Task Force Six commander.

verification.notes: Transcript context shows Owens reading Myers' account that a cartel member in Naco recited private details from his clearance packet. Current searches for Myers, Joint Task Force Six, Naco, the claimed clearance packet, and cartel contact found no authenticated packet, contemporaneous report, named witness, court filing, or independent account. Public episode summaries repeat the allegation but do not independently corroborate it. Missing public evidence is not a contradiction, so the claim remains unverifiable.
